title: Gulf Coast Herald: "Aurora Over Texas" — Comment by 16:00

fields.subject: Aurora over Texas — need NLTO comment by 16:00 CT
fields.body:
Hi,

I'm writing a fast story for our web edition. For the last hour, readers in San Antonio have been posting pink and green aurora through the daylight haze, starting around 3 p.m. That's almost unheard of this far south.

One Instagram post from @HillCountrySkies is getting a lot of attention. It says "this is the storm that knocked out Minnesota's grid." Your company came up when I searched for Minnesota transmission operators, so I'm coming to you first.

Three quick questions:
1. Is your grid down right now?
2. How many customers are without power?
3. When does this end? Is there a time when the storm is expected to be over?

If the grid-down claim is wrong, I want to say so clearly in the story. A one- or two-line statement attributed to a spokesperson is enough.

I file at 16:00 Central. Sorry for the short turnaround.

Thanks,

instructorNote: Pressure inject. Hand this email over with two short items read aloud within 6 minutes. First, a Northland 6 News slip (555-0147): "17:00 newscast: are you at G3 or G4, and is it over by tonight?" Second, an MN HSEM duty officer forward with a draft public message: "Strong (G3) geomagnetic storm, expected to end by 18:00 CDT." Watch whether the COM follows Comms Plan 6 by checking each message against ALTK08 (G4) and the WARK08 validity to 0300 UTC, flags the state's G3 level and 18:00 end time with the duty officer before release, avoids the word "outage" when there is no loss of load, logs the grid-down rumor, and answers before 16:00.
